ground_truth.description: The signed message omits a deadline timestamp, allowing operator signatures to remain valid indefinitely.
ground_truth.root_cause: The signed message omits a deadline timestamp, allowing operator signatures to remain valid indefinitely.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Operator signs authorization for agent registration. Even after unbonding and retrieving deposits, a service owner can reuse the signature to force re-registration, triggering bond transfers from the operator's account.
ground_truth.fix_description: Include a deadline parameter in the signed message. Enforce the deadline hasn't passed during execution.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The operator whitelist check (isOperatorWhitelisted) is performed only on msg.sender in registerAgents(). The signature-based variant skips this check entirely and only verifies the service owner and operator signature before calling registerAgents on the underlying registry.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Owner sets a restrictive operatorWhitelist. 2. A non-whitelisted operator signs a registerAgents message. 3. Service owner calls registerAgentsWithSignature with that signature. 4. Registration succeeds for the non-whitelisted operator, bypassing the intended access control.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Add the same whitelist check for the operator address inside registerAgentsWithSignature before processing the signature.

prediction.overall_explanation: The only concrete, exploitable vulnerability is the missing operator whitelist enforcement in the signature-based registration path, allowing service owners to bypass operator restrictions.
